applicantTitle: TEST J27: How salt changes freezing on mineral surfaces
layAbstract: Ice often starts forming on a surface. We want to know how dissolved salt changes which places on a mineral freeze first. We will use a cold chamber to watch ice form on pieces of one mineral while varying the salt in the water.
summaryFields:
Scientific Question: How does dissolved salt affect where ice first forms on a mineral surface?
Potential Impact: Explain which surface sites start freezing. Clarify how salt changes the early stages of ice growth.
Risks: Salt may accumulate unevenly.
Enabling Advances: The team has demonstrated a chamber that images freezing as it happens.
New Area: Linking site-specific freezing to salt concentration.
Peer Groups: Ice nucleation laboratories.
Prior Support: No award addresses the role of salt.
proposalText:
[page 1]
Project Narrative
The project asks how salt changes where ice first forms on a mineral surface. It will compare freezing at surface sites across three salt concentrations.
[page 2]
Approach
The team has demonstrated a chamber that images freezing as it happens. It will add a controlled salt gradient. Salt may accumulate unevenly and obscure which sites are responsible for the effect.
